title: August and the Bakery
premise: August Reyes, a baker who fled a powerful family's shadow a decade ago, has built a quiet life in the coastal town of Gullhaven, measuring safety in loaves and small kindnesses. When Astrid Dunmore finds an undelivered letter in her late grandfather's lighthouse—postmarked eleven years ago and addressed to August—the past he buried arrives on her doorstep. As they trace the letter's journey together, August must confront the corrupt family empire that once destroyed his father and decide whether survival is worth a half-lived life. When his brother arrives to reclaim him for the family's final consolidation of power, August chooses to stand, testify, and lose everything except what matters: Astrid, the bakery community that became his found family, and a whole heart finally risked.
about_author: Felix Pemberton is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded pre-dawn ovens for pre-dawn manuscripts after twenty years in kitchens across three coastlines. He writes love stories about people rebuilding themselves from flour, salt water, and second chances.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Wall
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. While restoring her grandfather's lighthouse, Astrid pries loose a tin box containing an eleven-year-old letter addressed to 'A. Reyes, the bakery.' She recognizes the name: the quiet baker she's watched from the pier for two years. The beat is curiosity sharpening into unease—someone hid this letter deliberately.

chapters.title: Sourdough and Small Steps
chapters.summary: August's POV. August's careful morning routine at the bakery establishes his self-imposed rules: no last names given, no past discussed, nothing owned that can be taken. Astrid arrives with the letter and watches his hands go still over the dough. The beat is terror wearing the mask of politeness as he refuses to open it.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Astrid reads enough of the envelope's return address to recognize the Reyes name from old financial scandals; August admits only that his family 'does things to people.' They agree—uneasily—to find out how the letter reached the lighthouse. The beat is reluctant alliance, two guarded people circling the same wound.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: August's POV. The letter, finally opened, is from August's father, written before his death in a 'accident' tied to the family company—and it names August as the heir who could stop them. Flashbacks reveal why August ran. The beat is grief resurfacing as rage, and the first crack in his policy of forgetting.

chapters.title: The Regulars
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A chapter of warmth: the bakery's found family—retired fisherman Dev, teenage apprentice Marisol, insomniac nurse Priya—rally around Astrid when her novel deadline collapses. Through their stories Astrid sees what August built here and why it must be protected. The beat is tenderness raising the stakes.

chapters.title: His Brother's Car
chapters.summary: August's POV. Julian Reyes arrives in Gullhaven, charming the town while privately offering August a choice: sign away his claim and stay hidden, or come home and be absorbed. Julian hints he knows about Astrid. The beat is dread—the corruption reaching into the one place August thought untouchable.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. August and Astrid fall into a tender, tentative romance, but August keeps withholding—dates, details, the truth about the threat. Astrid, who rebuilt her own life after loss, calls it out: he's lending pieces of himself, never risking the whole. The beat is intimacy colliding with honesty; she walks out.

chapters.title: Fire and Leverage
chapters.summary: August's POV. A suspicious fire guts the bakery; insurance records show Julian's fingerprints. Dev is hurt saving Marisol. August realizes hiding was never survival—it just moved the target onto everyone he loves. The beat is rock bottom transforming into resolve: he will testify, expose the company, and finish his father's letter's work.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the eve of testimony, August asks Astrid not for forgiveness but partnership—full truth, whole heart, whatever comes. The town's found family becomes his evidence network: Priya's records, Dev's contacts, Marisol's recovered files. The beat is courage chosen together, with time running out before the hearing.

chapters.title: August and the Bakery
chapters.summary: August's POV, closing with Astrid's epilogue voice. August testifies; the empire cracks, Julian falls, and August loses the inheritance but keeps the name on his own terms. Months later, the rebuilt bakery reopens with Astrid's novel on its counter. The beat is resolution: survival's price paid, and a life measured now in whole hearts, not safe steps.
